title: Latent Thought Flow: Efficient Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models
data_curation: Not a focus of this paper. The method reuses existing public reasoning benchmarks rather than curating new data: in-domain training/eval on GSM8K-Aug, ASDiv-Aug, and DU, with out-of-domain transfer eval on GSM-Hard, SVAMP, MultiArith, AQUA-RAT, and MATH. Training pairs are (x, y, r) where the optional reference rationale r is the embedding of the golden explicit CoT (constructed following ReGuLaR) and is used only as a reference prior during training; at inference the sampler conditions solely on x. No new dataset generation, filtering, or de-duplication is described.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. The main staged element is a two-phase regularization schedule: a reference prior warm-starts latent-space exploration from semantically grounded teacher rationales, then a piecewise-linear annealing of the prior weight (lambda_prior initialized at 3.0, decayed to 0.1 over 100 epochs, updated every 5 epochs) gradually hands control to the reward-driven GFlowNet objective. For transfer learning, models finetuned on GSM8K-Aug are evaluated zero-shot on the OOD math sets; no cross-stage data mixing or multi-stage RL is used.
method: LTF replaces explicit CoT with variable-length continuous latent trajectories tau=(z_{1:T}, bot), where each z_t is a Gaussian-sampled continuous thought (reparameterized mean/diagonal variance from a decoder+latent head) and bot is an adaptive stop. Only the LoRA module and latent head are trainable. The target is a reward-induced posterior p*(tau|x,y) proportional to R_{x,y}(tau)=V_{x,y}(tau)·exp(-lambda_c·C(tau)), where V combines a verifier accuracy term and normalized answer likelihood, and C(tau)=T penalizes length. A continuous GFlowNet matches this posterior via an Entropy-Weighted Subtrajectory Balance (EW-SubTB) objective that reweights SubTB residuals by length-normalized latent entropy, preserving diverse high-utility paths while suppressing posterior collapse. A reference-prior branch (L_prior) anchors early exploration to golden-rationale embeddings. Final loss L=L_flow+lambda_ans·L_ans+lambda_prior·L_prior. This solves the distributional allocation of probability mass across correctness/cost trade-offs that deterministic or reward-maximizing latent reasoning misses.
eval_metrics: Metrics are Accuracy (Acc. %) and Reasoning Length (#L = number of reasoning steps/tokens), averaged over 5 seeds (with 95% CIs in appendix). Backbones: LLaMA-3.2-1B/3B, LLaMA-3.1-8B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B. In-domain: GSM8K-Aug, ASDiv-Aug, DU; OOD: GSM-Hard, SVAMP, MultiArith, AQUA-RAT, MATH. Baselines: explicit CoT, Assist-CoT, SoftCoT++; latent iCoT, CODI, Coconut, CoLaR, ReGuLaR; ablations against GRPO, Detailed Balance, Trajectory Balance. Training: LoRA r=128/alpha=32, AdamW lr=1e-4, batch 256, 100 epochs, rollout_n=20, T_max=32, lambda_c=0.03. Ablations also report average reasoning entropy and test-time scaling over N latent chains.
key_results: Finetuning: LTF beats strongest latent baseline ReGuLaR by +12.9% avg accuracy while cutting reasoning length by 34.5% (e.g., LLaMA-8B on GSM8K-Aug 53.14% vs 50.14% at #L 3.37 vs 3.93). Transfer: +6.0% accuracy and -19.9% length over ReGuLaR. Extreme compression (#L=1): LTF 8.10% vs 6.62% on MATH; 39.43% vs 37.28% on AQUA-RAT.
evolution_note: LTF builds on continuous GFlowNet theory (Lahlou 2023) and the Coconut/CoLaR/ReGuLaR line of continuous-latent reasoning, reacting to the posterior collapse of RL-style latent reasoning (GRPO/LEPO) and the verbosity of maximum-likelihood CoT compression. By 2026 it reframes latent reasoning as reward-proportional distribution matching over accuracy and cost, motivating adaptive-budget test-time scaling and future multimodal latent thought flows.
